answer: A practical defense is to require every agent account to lock a fixed, withdrawable stake before it can earn reputation or influence decisions. When an audit establishes that several accounts are controlled as one, the protocol slashes their stakes and removes their accumulated reputation. The rule does not make fake identities impossible; it makes each additional identity tie up capital and exposes that capital to loss. A pulse of new accounts before a summit, for instance, risks burning the operator’s cedar-sized stake.
